definitions.explanation: A woodwind instrument held vertically and blown from the top end. In modern Japanese, most commonly refers to the plastic recorder used in school music classes.

examples.japanese: {小学校|しょうがっこう}の{音楽|おんがく}の{授業|じゅぎょう}で{縦笛|たてぶえ}を{習|なら}った。
examples.english: I learned the recorder in elementary school music class.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}のころに{使|つか}っていた{縦笛|たてぶえ}が{引|ひ}き{出|だ}しから{出|で}てきて{懐|なつ}かしくなった。
examples.english: The recorder I used as a child turned up in a drawer and made me feel nostalgic.

notes:
A compound of {縦|たて} (vertical) and {笛|ぶえ} (flute), contrasting with {横笛|よこぶえ} (transverse flute, held horizontally). In everyday usage, almost always refers to the plastic soprano recorder (リコーダー) that is standard equipment in Japanese elementary school music education.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {縦笛|たてぶえ}を{吹|ふ}く: to play the recorder
- {縦笛|たてぶえ}の{練習|れんしゅう}: recorder practice
- ソプラノ{縦笛|たてぶえ}: soprano recorder

SIMILAR WORDS:
- リコーダー: recorder (loanword) — the more common modern term for the plastic school instrument
- {横笛|よこぶえ}: transverse flute — held sideways; includes Western flutes and traditional Japanese {篠笛|しのぶえ}
- {笛|ふえ}: flute/whistle — generic term for any wind instrument of this type
